The morning light falls soft across the small blue room.
A coffee cup waits cold beside the quiet open window.
Dust motes drift slowly through the pale golden morning air.
I stretch my thin arms toward the bright gray ceiling.
The floorboards creak beneath my bare and sleepy feet now.
My shadow lengthens quietly onto the worn and pale rug.
The kettle sings a brief sharp note inside the kitchen.
Outside, a neighbor laughs, and the sound feels distant today.
The sky is wide, pale, and full of thin clouds.
I breathe slowly, watching the pale world become awake now.

An old song enters through the open window softly here.
I remember summers when the lake was full of light.
Friends laughed at the shore, their voices fading slow now.
The water held reflections of trees and moving clouds above.
We built a small house from driftwood by the path.
Rain washed the dust from our tired muddy shoes again.
Night fell early, and stars appeared like cold silver needles.
We whispered secrets into the dark and trusted them then.
Time moved gently, carrying us away from that shore quietly.
Now I hear only the quiet and the rain outside.

I return to my desk and open the old laptop.
The screen glows blue, filling the small dark room softly.
Words appear on paper, but they feel thin and cold.
I write a sentence, erase it, then write another one.
The clock ticks softly, counting minutes that do not hurry.
My chair turns slowly as I lean toward the window.
The city hums below, a low murmur of life now.
A phone lights up, then goes dark on the desk.
I imagine sending a message, but I leave it unread.
The day waits patiently, asking nothing, offering only time now.

I make a simple bowl of rice and warm broth.
Steam rises from the spoon, carrying the smell of salt.
The broth tastes like home, though home is far away.
A lemon slice sits bright against the white ceramic plate.
I sip slowly, listening to the quiet rain continue again.
The rain falls steady against the glass, like soft fingers.
My stomach warms, and the room feels less empty now.
Bread crumbles on the table, a quiet golden snow soft.
I save half the bread for tomorrow, vague and far.
The bowl becomes empty; I carry it to the sink.

The sky darkens slowly, losing its last pale light now.
Streetlamps blink on along the wet and quiet street below.
A cat crosses the road, its small shadow stretching long.
The building breathes around me, pipes and old wooden floors.
My lamp gives a circle of yellow warmth here now.
The chair feels soft beneath my tired and aching bones.
I close my eyes, letting the silence become a blanket.
Thoughts drift like slow boats on a dark river below.
One thought says fear, another says let it pass now.
I choose quiet, simple, possible, kind, now, and rest again.

I walk to the window and watch the streetlights shine.
Each window in the buildings holds a small warm glow.
Some windows are dark, waiting for their people to sleep.
A woman carries her umbrella, her reflection blurred by rain.
A man stops under the awning, reading a newspaper slowly.
The street becomes a river of light and wet stone.
I press my cold hand against the cool glass there.
For a moment, the world seems close enough to touch.
Then the rain shifts, and the lights begin to blur.
I step back inside, carrying the night with me again.

A radio crackles, then offers a slow, warm tune tonight.
The melody moves through the room like a soft tide.
I hum along, though the words are old and strange.
The singer sounds far away, but the music feels near.
My feet tap lightly to the quiet beat on floor.
The rhythm is simple, patient, and enough to hold me.
It carries memory without asking me to name it now.
I remember dancing once under a blue summer moon light.
The floor moved, and my heart seemed to fly up.
Now the radio fades, and the silence returns gently home.

I think about the dreams that visit while I sleep.
In one, I walk through a garden made of glass.
Each flower rings softly when the cool evening wind blows.
In another dream, I fly above a silver sea below.
The sky is full of birds with bright white wings.
They carry small lights, and the lights become stars above.
I reach for them, but my hands pass through air.
The dream becomes a question, soft and impossible to answer.
It asks me to remember what I cannot hold now.
Then I wake, and the room is still quiet here.

The clock says late, though my body feels early now.
I rise, stretch, and move toward the pale window there.
The rain has stopped, and the street smells fresh today.
Puddles hold the sky, small silver mirrors on wet stone.
A bicycle passes, its wheel catching the early sun bright.
Someone sweeps leaves along the curb, making soft sounds there.
The city begins to hum with voices and engines now.
I put on a coat, buttoning it in the cold.
The door opens, and the cool air touches my face.
I step outside, leaving the quiet room behind me now.

The sidewalk glistens, black and bright beneath my shoes again.
Each step sends small ripples through the shallow water there.
A bus passes, then another, filling the street bright now.
People hurry, but I walk slowly into morning now again.
The air smells clean, a little sweet, a little cold.
I look up and see the sky opening slowly again.
A white bird crosses the light, then vanishes quietly away.
I smile, though I cannot name the reason for it.
The day asks nothing, except that I keep moving now.
And so I walk on, with the morning beside me.
